standard.title: Develop questions about systems
standard.description: develop questions to investigate people, events, developments, places and systems
standard.prior_knowledge: From AC9HS5S01 (Develop system investigation questions): Students develop purposeful inquiry questions using probing, open-ended and practical question types. Students can frame inquiry questions across HASS stages.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions to investigate people, events, developments, places and systems, including ethical and system-level questions that reveal connections across economic, political and environmental dimensions.

nodes.label: Ethical and systemic question types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop ethical questions about cultural protocol and sensitivity, and system-mapping questions that reveal connections between economic, political and environmental systems.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop one ethical question and one question that reveals a connection between two HASS systems.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a range of question types for Year 6 contexts: probing questions, open-ended questions, practical questions for enterprising behaviours, and ethical questions about cultural sensitivities and protocol. Develop questions that reveal connections across systems (e.g. 'How do the purchases my family makes influence the environment?').
wider: Mind-map a complex HASS concept (e.g. consumer decisions and environmental impact) and generate questions that reveal all significant system connections
Develop an inquiry question set that requires investigation across at least two HASS disciplines and explain how each question targets a different disciplinary lens
nodes.hinge_reason: Ethical questions and system-level questions are the Year 6 extensions beyond Year 5 practice — students who cannot form these question types will conduct surface-level inquiries that miss the systemic connections that Year 6 content demands.

response_modes.reason: Model ethical and system-level questions explicitly, showing the difference between 'what happened?' and 'who is affected and why?' — students need to see the form of these questions before generating them independently.

success_criteria: Students develop at least one ethical question relevant to a HASS inquiry.
Students develop at least one question that reveals a connection between two systems or disciplines.

nodes.label: Questions that guide all inquiry stages
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a set of questions that frame and guide all stages of a HASS inquiry — before, during and after investigation — addressing relevant disciplinary concepts.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop a set of at least four questions that cover different stages of a HASS inquiry using at least two question types.
nodes.typical_width: Develop questions that address relevant disciplinary concepts before, during and after investigation; include probing, open-ended, practical and ethical question types; ensure questions guide investigation toward evidence-based conclusions.
wider: Develop questions for a multi-disciplinary inquiry that spans history, geography and economics, showing how each question targets a specific disciplinary concept
Evaluate a completed set of inquiry questions after investigation — assessing which questions generated the most productive inquiry and why

response_modes.reason: Build a question bank across multiple Year 6 inquiry topics — students improve at question design through varied practice, not repetition of the same topic.

success_criteria: Students develop at least four inquiry questions covering different stages and purposes.
Students use at least two question types including at least one ethical or systemic question.

nodes.label: Complete inquiry question set for Year 6 topics
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a complete inquiry question set for a Year 6 HASS topic that spans disciplines, addresses cultural sensitivities, and guides investigation from initial framing through to conclusions and action.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop a complete question set (minimum 5 questions) for a Year 6 HASS topic that includes at least one ethical question.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a complete inquiry question set for a Year 6 topic (e.g. Federation, migration, consumer choices, international interconnections) that: frames investigation stages, addresses disciplinary concepts across multiple HASS areas, includes ethical and systemic questions, and guides toward evidence-based conclusions.
wider: Design a question set for a community-based inquiry project that requires real data collection, and evaluate how each question supports the project's goals
Revisit and refine questions mid-inquiry based on what has been found so far — modelling iterative professional inquiry practice

response_modes.reason: A complete Year 6 inquiry question set requires integrating all question types across all disciplines — the quality measure is coherence and coverage, not just the number of questions.

success_criteria: Students develop at least five questions covering different stages and types for a Year 6 HASS inquiry.
Questions include at least one ethical question and one question revealing system connections.
The question set addresses at least two HASS disciplines.
